title: Apple pays Google ~$1B/yr for Siri's brain
blurb: The "privacy-first" brand will license Gemini and host a custom 1.2-trillion-parameter model on Google infrastructure — while collecting $20B/yr from Google for search.
body:
Apple — which built a decade of identity on privacy ("what happens on your iPhone stays on your iPhone") — is reported to be paying Google ~$1 billion a year to license Gemini AI and host a custom 1.2-trillion-parameter model on Google infrastructure to power Siri.

The financial picture is wilder still: Google simultaneously pays Apple ~$20 billion a year to remain the default iPhone search engine — roughly 20% of Apple's Services revenue, its main growth segment. So Apple collects Google's largest distribution payment and pays Google to power its flagship AI feature, at the same time.

The contradiction is sharp: Apple's software chief had previously banned engineers from Google Cloud over privacy. The take: it signals Apple's vertical-integration bet cracking under AI's compute demands — when the privacy promise meets the arms race, the arms race wins.

SOURCE · Zachary Boland, LinkedIn commentary on reported Apple–Google deal.
